summary: This lecture supplies the core anti-Homer and Trojan-horse inversion layer for the Aeneid cluster: Rome cannot erase Homer from memory, so the Aeneid enters Homeric scenes and reverses their moral charge until Greek culture, mercy, and love feel dangerous while piety and empire feel saving.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The public read already links the anti-Homer and real-Trojan-horse marks to the Stories anchor.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The active mechanism is inherited-world inversion: Rome keeps Homeric memory alive but recodes Greek beauty, rhetoric, theater, mercy, and love as corrupting threats.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The public read already links Priam and Achilles' grief opening into recognition to the Human Heart anchor.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Human Heart owns the positive counter-measure: the Iliad scene lets enemy grief reveal personhood before Virgil reverses that mercy into gullibility.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The public read already links the anti-Homer reversal of enemy reconciliation to the battlefield-forgiveness anchor.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This is the same love-and-forgiveness test from the negative side: a civilizational story trains readers to feel that forgiving an enemy is weakness.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already absorbed in public prose: this is the clearest current source for the Trojan-horse inversion mechanism, where a rival poetic world cannot be burned because it lives in memory, so imperial narrative keeps the old scenes while reversing what love, mercy, speech, and Greek culture mean.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Stories owns the inversion of an inherited world; Poetry owns memorized verse and civilizational medium; Human Heart owns the positive love/forgiveness measure; Guide Trap owns Virgil's later role as necessary false guide; Legitimacy Fiction owns the Augustan authorization layer.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already absorbed as an anti-test: Priam and Achilles show enemy-recognition and forgiveness as higher civilization, while the Aeneid turns that mercy into stupidity and makes love look like the cause of civilizational destruction.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Human Heart gets this only where the operative question is whether love and forgiveness recognize a concrete person or enemy soul; Stories gets the narrative machinery that poisons that recognition.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this source as Poetry evidence when the active mechanism is memorized epic becoming the infrastructure of a people's mental world and a poem becoming an engine of civilization through values, not plot.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Poetry should not absorb the whole anti-Homer inversion sequence; that would duplicate Stories' narrower claim about rival-world reversal.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold as supporting evidence only when the active mechanism is Augustus needing an imperial bible, not when the active mechanism is how an inherited poetic world is morally inverted from inside.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Legitimacy Fiction owns authorization, descent, prophecy, and imperial right; Stories owns the educational and emotional recoding by which the authorized story remakes the reader's world.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-03-18 Great Books lecture sits between the 2024-12-05 David/Bible lecture, where the Aeneid appears as a kingship and legitimacy comparison, and the 2026-03-25 Poetry of Empire lecture, where the same anti-Homer mechanism becomes inner imperial training.

The source strengthens but does not settle the Imperial Poetry And Trojan-Horse Inversion child question. The live boundary proposal still keeps the mechanism on the Stories parent unless a redistribution with Poetry, Guide Trap, Human Heart, and Legitimacy Fiction would reduce duplication.

next_actions.action: No immediate public lens prose mutation is needed. How Stories Control Reality already cites this source in the Aeneid section and exposes the durable stories-trojan-horse-inverts-inherited-world anchor.
